name: Seely Avenue Mixed-Use
acresNote: About 22 acres (notice of determination, Aug 2024; Draft EIR p. 8): APNs 097-15-033 and 097-15-034 and part of 097-66-004, bounded by Seely Avenue, Montague Expressway, Coyote Creek and Epic Way. The County has since replaced those parcels with the project's own lots; drawn from them, the site comes to about 22.2 acres.

program.notes: As approved: 1,472 homes in three-story townhomes and six- to seven-story apartment buildings, 18,965 sq ft of neighborhood retail and a 2.5-acre public park, plus about 0.11 acre dedicated to the San José Municipal Water System for a new well (notice of determination, Aug 13, 2024). The Draft EIR splits the homes into 154 for-sale townhomes; Buildings A, B and C with 397, 372 and 371 market-rate apartments over ground-floor retail; and a 178-home affordable apartment building (Tables 2-1 and 2-3; Table 2-4 gives Building A 399). Heights: Building A 69 ft (six stories), Buildings B and C 79 ft (seven stories), the affordable building 82 ft and the townhomes 30 ft (Table 2-2). The park is 2.51 acres in the Draft EIR. Parking is in garages beside the apartment buildings, not underground.

publicPartners: San José Municipal Water System (well site)
stageNote: Approved. The San José City Council approved the Planned Development rezoning and permit on Aug 13, 2024, finding the Final EIR complete and adopting a statement of overriding considerations for the impacts on historical resources. The County's parcel map now shows the project's lots, but no building permit or construction record could be checked.

timeline.event: San José circulates a notice of preparation for an EIR: 1,470 homes, about 52,000 sq ft of retail and a 2.5-acre park on about 22 acres.
The Draft EIR is released for comment; it is recirculated from Mar 19 to May 3, 2024 because some appendices hadn't been posted correctly.
The City Council approves the project with its Final EIR: 1,472 homes, 18,965 sq ft of retail and a 2.5-acre public park.

summary: About 22 acres of farmland on Seely Avenue in North San José, beside Coyote Creek and Montague Expressway, approved in 2024 for 1,472 homes: three six- and seven-story apartment buildings with shops facing a new 2.5-acre public park, a 178-home affordable building and 154 townhomes. The farm's buildings, including the Sakauye house, form a potential historic district associated with Japanese farming in the Santa Clara Valley, which the project would remove.
massingNotes: Added at Matthew's request (2026-10-19). Boundary (data/boundaries/seely-avenue.geojson, approximate): the approval's APNs are no longer in the County's layer, so the site is drawn from the Santa Clara County parcels (data.sccgov.org ubcd-cewv) that replaced them, which are the project's own lots (Buildings A, B and C, the affordable building, the park and the well site match the Draft EIR's lot areas within 2%), with the 26 townhome lots and the unnumbered street and common lots; 22.2 acres. Illustrative massing (data/massing/seely-avenue.geojson, pipeline/bam_pipeline/sites/massing_seely_avenue.py): each building's lot raised to its Draft EIR height (Table 2-2): Building A 69 ft, Buildings B and C 79 ft, the affordable building 82 ft and the 26 townhome lots 30 ft, matched to the lots by area (Table 2-1) and by position on the conceptual site plan (Figure 2-4). The lots also hold each building's garage and courtyards, so these are envelopes, not footprints. All stage entitled.
